proof:
# No finite linear Brunn–Minkowski compensation for two paired centroid tails

**Exact counterexample in dimension two.** For equal-area planar convex bodies \(A,D\), no finite constant \(c_2\) can make

\[
 F_A(s)+F_D(-s)+c_2\left(\frac{|(A+D)/2|}{|A|}-1\right)
                                      \ge2\gamma_2=\frac89  \tag{1}
\]

hold for every direction and shift. Each tail in (1) is measured from its body's own ordinary centroid. The counterexample also works with both caps measured from \((g_A+g_D)/2\), after the explicit shift conversion in Section 3. All bodies in the construction are full-dimensional rational trapezoids with the same four edge directions.

This does not contradict the proved same-body paired-tail theorem. It disproves a linear volume-deficit extension to different equal-volume bodies, not the mixed-integer conjecture.

## 1. A fixed-normal equal-area family

For a rational parameter \(w>1\), define

\[
 h(w)=\frac{w+w^{-1}}2,\qquad
 \ell(w)=\frac{w-w^{-1}}2,
\]

\[
 K_w=\{(x,y):\ell(w)\le x\le h(w),\quad |y|\le x/2\}.
\]

Its four vertices are \((\ell,\pm\ell/2)\) and \((h,\pm h/2)\), all rational. It is a compact convex body, its vertical width at coordinate \(x\) is \(x\), and

\[
 |K_w|=\frac{h(w)^2-\ell(w)^2}{2}=\frac12.
\]

By symmetry the centroid has second coordinate zero. Its first coordinate is

\[
 m(w)=\frac23\bigl(h(w)^3-\ell(w)^3\bigr)
     =\frac w2+\frac1{6w^3}.                               \tag{2}
\]

Thus every member has exactly the same area, without a volume approximation or an implicit rescaling.

For two parameters \(u,v>1\), the Minkowski midpoint is exactly

\[
 \frac{K_u+K_v}{2}
 =\left\{(x,y):\frac{\ell(u)+\ell(v)}2\le x\le
                       \frac{h(u)+h(v)}2,\quad |y|\le x/2\right\}.
\]

Indeed, at any admissible sum of first coordinates, the summed interval widths add to that same first coordinate. Consequently

\[
 \boxed{\ \frac{|(K_u+K_v)/2|}{|K_u|}-1
      =\frac14\left(\frac uv+\frac vu-2\right)
      =\frac{(u-v)^2}{4uv}.\ }                              \tag{3}
\]

## 2. The rational perturbation and its deficit

Let \(0<\varepsilon\le1/100\) be rational and set

\[
 v=1+\varepsilon,\qquad
 u=1+\varepsilon+2\varepsilon^2,
 \qquad A=K_u,\quad D=K_v.
\]

These are opposite parameter perturbations, of size \(\varepsilon^2\), about \(K_{1+\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2}\). In particular both remain in the same fixed-normal trapezoid family. Formula (3) gives the exact relative volume excess

\[
 \boxed{\ \delta_\varepsilon
       =\frac{\varepsilon^4}{uv}\le\varepsilon^4.\ }         \tag{4}
\]

As \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), both bodies approach the triangle
\(K_1=\{0\le x\le1,\ |y|\le x/2\}\), whose increasing triangular section profile attains paired-tail equality at a nonzero shift.

## 3. The actual paired closed caps

Use direction \(e_1\), and put

\[
 L(w)=h(w)-m(w)=\frac1{2w}-\frac1{6w^3},
 \qquad s=L(u)>0.
\]

The closed cap of \(A\) at own-centroid threshold \(s\) is
\(\{x\ge m(u)+s=h(u)\}\); it is its supporting vertical edge and has area zero. The cap of \(D\) at the opposite own-centroid threshold is

\[
 \{x\ge m(v)-s\}=\{x\ge t\},\qquad
 t=m(v)+m(u)-h(u).
\]

It is a proper cap. To verify this without an asymptotic argument, define

\[
 t_0=2m(v)-h(v),\qquad \Delta=L(v)-L(u)>0,
 \quad t=t_0+\Delta.
\]

We have \(t_0\ge1/3\), since \(t_0(1)=1/3\) and

\[
 t_0'(w)=\frac{(w^2-1)(w^2+2)}{2w^4}\ge0.
\]

Also \(\ell(v)\le\varepsilon\le1/100\). Hence \(t>\ell(v)\). On the other hand, \(L(u)>0\), and

\[
 t<m(v)\le\frac{101}{200}+\frac16=\frac{403}{600}<1\le h(v).
\]

The exact normalized paired cost is therefore

\[
                  F_A(s)+F_D(-s)=h(v)^2-t^2.                \tag{5}
\]

For the common-centroid convention, write
\(g=(m(u)+m(v))/2\) and choose \(s_{\rm common}=h(u)-g>0\). The two thresholds are then \(g+s_{\rm common}=h(u)\) and \(g-s_{\rm common}=t\), exactly the same caps. Thus no centroid offset is suppressed. Positivity of this common shift follows from \(g<1\le h(u)\), using (2) and \(u<51/50\).

## 4. A uniform exact lower bound on the shortfall

For a single member \(K_v\), the paired cost at its own corresponding nonzero shift satisfies the exact identity

\[
 h(v)^2-t_0^2
             =\frac89+\frac{(v^2-1)^3}{9v^6}.               \tag{6}
\]

The small positive term is cubic in \(\varepsilon\), not quadratic. The two-body perturbation decreases the cost in (6) by \(2t_0\Delta+\Delta^2\). Thus the shortfall below \(8/9\) is

\[
 S_\varepsilon
 :=\frac89-F_A(s)-F_D(-s)
 =2t_0\Delta+\Delta^2-\frac{(v^2-1)^3}{9v^6}.               \tag{7}
\]

Now

\[
 -L'(w)=\frac{w^2-1}{2w^4},
\]

so positivity and \(v\le w\le u\) give

\[
 \Delta=\int_v^u\frac{w^2-1}{2w^4}\,dw
 \ge\frac{(v^2-1)(u-v)}{2u^4}
 =\frac{\varepsilon^3(2+\varepsilon)}{u^4}.                \tag{8}
\]

Use \(t_0\ge1/3\), \(u\le51/50\), \(v\ge1\), and
\(2+\varepsilon\le201/100\). Equations (7)–(8) imply

\[
 S_\varepsilon
 \ge\left(\frac4{3(51/50)^4}
                   -\frac{(201/100)^3}{9}\right)\varepsilon^3
 >\frac{\varepsilon^3}{4}.                                \tag{9}
\]

The last strict inequality is entirely rational: the bracket minus \(1/4\) is

\[
                  \frac{1613599914733}{20295603000000}>0.
\]

Combining (4) and (9),

\[
 \boxed{\ \frac{2\gamma_2-F_A(s)-F_D(-s)}
                    {|(A+D)/2|/|A|-1}
                         >\frac1{4\varepsilon}\to\infty.\ }\tag{10}
\]

Given any finite proposed \(c_2\ge0\), choose an integer
\(N>\max\{100,4c_2\}\) and \(\varepsilon=1/N\). The explicitly rational polygons above then violate (1). Closed supporting-cap boundary mass is exactly zero under area measure, and the other cap is strictly proper, so no open/closed limiting convention is needed.

The rational functions additionally give
\(S_\varepsilon=(4/9)\varepsilon^3+O(\varepsilon^4)\) and
\(\delta_\varepsilon=\varepsilon^4+O(\varepsilon^5)\); these asymptotics are explanatory only. The proof of divergence uses the exact inequalities (4) and (9).

## 5. What the obstruction separates

The bodies are equal-area, have the same normal fan, and are arbitrarily close. Their Minkowski deficit is quadratic in the opposite parameter displacement. The same-body paired-tail slack at the limiting nonzero-shift triangular equality is only cubic in the apex truncation parameter. These two rates permit the perturbation to produce a cubic shortfall while paying only a quartic volume deficit.

This closes the proposed finite **linear** modulus already for \(d=2\). More generally, the same exact estimates rule out a uniform charge \(C\delta^\alpha\) for every exponent \(\alpha>3/4\): the shortfall-to-charge ratio is at least \(\varepsilon^{3-4\alpha}/4\), which diverges. No claim of sufficiency at exponent \(3/4\) is made. The example does not refute weaker nonlinear deficit bounds, a bound involving additional shape data, or a statement that also uses a middle source. It does not affect the exact transport identities in `candidate 68d3d3976d28a947` or the same-body paired-tail theorem.

The independent exact verifier is `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_planar_linear_bm_compensation_obstruction.py`.
